title: Finite local freeness of a given degree descends to a finite stage of a limit (Stacks 06AC)
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ ($X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]) and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$. If $f$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $f_i$ is finite locally free for some $i\ge0$; if moreover $f$ is finite locally free of degree $d$, then $f_i$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ for some $i\ge0$. (Stacks Project, Limits, Lemma Tag 06AC.)

source.place: Limits, Lemma Tag 06AC (lemma-descend-finite-locally-free) in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property), with its proof (Limits Lemmas descend-flat-finite-presentation and descend-finite-finite-presentation 01ZO, Morphisms Lemma finite-flat, Limits Lemma 05F4 limit-contained-in-constructible)

proof.text: The locally finite presentation hypothesis implies locally finite type: on each affine pair the target algebra is a quotient of a polynomial algebra in finitely many variables, so their images generate it [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The hypothesis that $f$ is finite locally free gives that $f$ is finite and flat by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] yields $a\ge0$ with $f_a$ finite, and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] yields $b\ge0$ with $f_b$ flat. Choose $i\ge a,b$. By cartesian-square pasting, $f_i$ is the base change of $f_a$ along $Y_i\to Y_a$, and of $f_b$ along $Y_i\to Y_b$. Finiteness and flatness are preserved by these base changes. Moreover $f_i$ is locally of finite presentation by base-change stability. Therefore $f_i$ is finite locally free by its definition.

source.place: Tag 06AC, label lemma-descend-finite-locally-free, first paragraph; the finite-generator observation spells out Morphisms 01TW

proof.text: Assume also that $f$ has degree $d$. The degree-local-constancy lemma gives the open and closed subset $W_d\subseteq Y_i$ where $f_i$ has degree $d$. The rank base-change formula applied to $f=f_i\times_{Y_i}Y$ says that its degree at $y\in Y$ equals the degree of $f_i$ at its image in $Y_i$. Hence $Y\to Y_i$ has image in $W_d$.

Apply the scheme-over-limit lemma to $Y_0\to S_0$: $Y$ is the limit of the $Y_j$, $j\ge0$, with affine transition maps. Each $Y_j\to Y_0$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated; since $Y_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so is $Y_j$ by qcqs permanence. An open and closed subset is retrocompact: its intersection with a quasi-compact open is closed therein and hence quasi-compact. Consequently $W_d$ is constructible, being itself a retrocompact open, by the constructible-subset definition. All hypotheses of the constructible-limit lemma are therefore satisfied, and it gives $i'\ge i$ such that $Y_{i'}\to Y_i$ has image in $W_d$.

proof.text: The morphism $f_{i'}$ is the base change of $f_i$ along $Y_{i'}\to Y_i$. It remains finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by the same permanence results as in Step 1. For every $y'\in Y_{i'}$, the rank base-change formula identifies its degree with that of $f_i$ at the image of $y'$, which lies in $W_d$ and therefore has degree $d$. Thus $f_{i'}$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free].
